newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Shell says Cornea find recovery rate key.
newsitem.headline: Shell says Cornea find recovery rate key.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group on Thursday hosed down the immediate significance of a potential big oil find offshore Western Australia announced by joint venture partner Cultus Petroleum NL, saying the recovery rate could be as low as five percent.
"It's central to combine the reserve estimate with the likely recovery rate, which is not known at this time," a spokeswoman for Shell subsidiary Shell Australia Ltd said.
"However, we believe it would be on the low side, perhaps in the five to 35 percent range," she said.
Shell is operator of the WA-241-P joint venture.
Cultus said earlier on Thursday that new estimates for its Cornea field indicated between 617 million and 2.665 billion barrels of oil were in place.
Shell previously indicated recoverable reserves of between 200 million and 400 million barrels.
Cultus share hit a record A$4.05 on the report, before easing back to A$3.94, up 24 cents.
Cultus company secretary Sam Russotti told Reuters in Wellington the recovery rate was likely to be less than 50 percent.

In a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange, Cultus said: "The determination of more precise oil in place volumetrics and oil recovery factors will be some of the objectives of the future exploration/appraisal programme."
Given the size of the reserve range coupled with an unknown recovery rate, Cultus "really should have emphasised the unknown recovery rate," the Shell spokeswoman said.
Analysts said the reservoir depth, permeability and the oil's heavy viscosity of 28 degrees API suggests a recovery rate on the low side.
Most Australian oil is of much lighter grades.
"The recovery rate could be as low as 10 or 15 percent," Peter Best of Macquarie Bank said.
At that rate, the actual amount of oil delivered by Cornea would be well below the 3.5 billion barrels estimated to have been recoverable from Australia's largest offshore field, Bass Strait.
The reserves are based on the first three wells drilled in the field with the estimated hydrocarbon columns which range from 22 to 50 metres and pressure data, Cultus said on Thursday.
Cultus said that the AC/P17 Joint Venture had secured the drill rig Sedco 703 and it would drill two exploration wells in the WA-241-P (Browse Basin) joint venture in the Cornea field.
The first of the wells will be Cornea South No.1 which is located on a southern lobe (possible extension) of the Cornea Structure and the estimated spud date is late June/early July.
The second well location will be determined upon results of the Cornea South No.1 well being known.

Shell Development has submitted to the WA-241-P/WA96-4 (WA-265-P)/WA96-5 (WA-266-P) Joint Ventures a forward exploration programme for the next 12 months consisting of a total of 13 wells and 2,100 sq km of 3D seismic acquisition.
Permit WA-241-P is operated by Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd with 50 percent, while Cultus and Chevron Corp unit Chevron Asiatic Ltd each hold 25 percent.
-- James Regan Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
